subject.title: fix(acpx): drain leased descendants when turns are aborted

question: Should OpenClaw make lease-verified host-process containment authoritative for ACPX cancellation and startup, even though that evicts reusable live handles and can block ACPX registration?
rationale: The implementation fixes a credentialed-process safety gap and appears correct, but automation cannot authorize the deliberate compatibility and availability tradeoff against upstream cooperative-cancel semantics.

options.title: Approve fail-closed containment
options.body: Accept live-handle eviction and startup refusal as the supported ACPX safety contract while preserving resumable session metadata.

options.title: Require recovery UX first
options.body: Keep strict containment but add a supported diagnostic or Doctor-style remediation path before merge.

options.title: Preserve existing semantics
options.body: Reject destructive cancellation and fail-closed startup and require a different containment design.

recommendation.title: Approve fail-closed containment
recommendation.body: Accept live-handle eviction and startup refusal as the supported ACPX safety contract while preserving resumable session metadata.

likelyOwner.reason: The affected manager/cache and ACPX lifecycle boundaries trace most strongly to this person's merged feature and refactor history.
